title: Optimized Setup and Protocol for Magnetic Domain Imaging with In Situ Hysteresis Measurement
protocol: Cut two U-shaped parts (Parts A and B) from the steel of interest using Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM).
Mount Part A in a hot-compression mount machine, ensuring transparency of the mount.
Place Part A into the mold with the legs facing upwards.
Add approximately 20 mL of methyl methacrylate compound powder to the mold.
Start the mounting cycle with heating time set for 4.5 min, cooling time for 4 min, pressure at 290 Bar, and temperature at 180 °C.
Retrieve the mount after completion of the cycle and check its thickness.
Ensure the final thickness is between 20 - 25 mm.
Grind the side of the mounted sample using 320 grit SiC paper on a grinding machine until the base of the legs is revealed.
Grind the other side of the mount and check frequently until the flat part of the U-shaped sample surface shows.
Measure the length of the revealed sample using a caliper and continue grinding carefully, measuring frequently.
Stop grinding as soon as the length reaches 25.05 ± 0.05 mm.
Polish the sample according to standard metallographic sample preparation procedures for soft steels.
Etch the polished sample using a cotton swab with suitable reagent for 1 - 5 s.
Check the etched sample under an optical microscope.
Polish the sample again using 1 µm diamond polishing agent until the etched surface layer is completely removed.
Repeat steps 2.6 to 2.8 for 4 - 6 times.
Finish the polishing using alumina suspension for 2 min.
Wrap a single layer, 50 turn coil around the longest side of Part B using 0.20 mm diameter enameled copper wire.
Leave around 100 mm of wire at each end of the coil.
Remove the enamel from the last 20 mm of each end of the wire using 800 grit sandpaper.
Check for electrical short circuits between coil and sample.
Take a multimeter and set it to test for continuity.
Touch one probe to Part B and the other to the end of one wire.
Install the front plate shown in Figure 2(a) on a flat surface.
Fit the mounted sample into the hole in the front plate.
Apply hot melt glue around the circumference of the mounted sample to secure it in place.
Insert Part B through the excitation coils into the bottom of the sample holder, ensuring that the sample protrudes from the top by about 1 mm.
Fix the back plate onto the back of the sample holder and loosely tighten the bottom nuts.
Align the Hall sensor with the sample visually.
Apply exciting current to the excitation coil to form an electromagnet for easy assembly and alignment.
Align Part A with Part B, using both magnetic force and visual inspection if the sample mount is transparent.
Bolt the top plate to the sample holder.
Tighten the bottom nuts to apply pressure between Part A and Part B without overtightening.
Level the sample for consistently good focusing across the field of vision.
Put a piece of modeling clay the size of a cherry onto a clean glass slide.
Place the test rig on top of the modeling clay with the sample approximately centered.
Place three sheets of lens tissue on top of the sample surface for protection.
Level the whole test rig using a levelling press for microscopy with the sample center aligned.
Draw 1 mL of oil-based ferro-fluid using a pipette and add it to a 5 mL vial.
Add 0.5 mL of hydrocarbon oil into the vial containing the ferro-fluid.
Shake the mixture for 10 seconds.
Draw a single drop (about 0.25 mL) of diluted ferro-fluid using a pipette.
Apply the ferro-fluid drop on the sample surface.
Place a clean microscope slide on top of the sample and slowly remove it to form a thin, uniform layer.
Observe the domain pattern under a light microscope before the ferro-fluid dries out.
Use ample lighting and adjust the aperture diaphragm for optimal contrast.
Attach a high-speed video camera to the microscope.
Apply a magnetic field to the sample to make the DWs move.
Securely fix the sample to the test rig.
Apply hot melt around the sample using a glue gun if necessary.
Connect up the in situ domain imaging system as shown.
Connect the sensor excitation coils to the power output of the BH analyzer.
Connect the Hall sensor to the H input channel of the BH analyzer.
Connect the sensor B coils to the B input channel of the BH analyzer.
Connect the H and B outputs of the BH analyzer to two analogue input channels of the Midas DA BNC Breakout box.
Connect the Sync In of the high-speed camera to the Sync Out of the DA box.
Connect the Trigger of the high-speed camera to the Trigger of the DA box.
Input the test parameters in the BH analyzer software.
Set the data sync parameters as per the instruction of the DA software.
Set the sync out rate (2,000/s) to be the frame rate (500 frame/s) of the high-speed camera multiplied by the number of data points per frame (4 per frame).
Set the pre-trigger length (in percentage) to be same as that of the camera.
Set the high-speed video camera ready for recording.
Turn on the BH analyzer and apply a 1 Hz excitation sinusoidal current to measure the major loop.
Check that the measured BH loop is roughly as expected in terms of coercive field, remanence, magnetic saturation, etc.
Trigger the camera either by sending a trigger signal from the BH analyzer or by clicking on the Trigger button on DA software interface.
Stop recording data and video after at least one BH loop cycle in the DA software.
Turn off the BH analyzer.
Do not keep the electric current running through the sample for a long time, especially if using direct current (DC).
Clean the sample after use.
Refresh the setup for future analysis.
